name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 18 points, among the bluest in Illinois
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson holds a roughly seven-to-one fundraising edge
Challenger Christian Maxwell is minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
model.rationale: The district's eighteen-point Democratic lean, Jackson's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising advantage leave Maxwell without a visible path, and markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Maxwell or an unexpected scandal involving Jackson could narrow the margin, though an upset would require an extraordinary shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, first elected in 2022, seeks a third term in a Chicago-area district that leans Democratic by about eighteen points. He has raised more than $418,000, far outpacing Republican Christian Maxwell, who has brought in roughly $63,000 and enters the fall with limited cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Jackson's chances near 95 percent.

The fundamentals point firmly toward Jackson: the district's partisan lean, his incumbency, and his financial edge all favor the Democrat. Maxwell would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or a major infusion of outside money to become competitive. As things stand, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin in November.
